papers.text: Paint on the bandstand: CONCERT SUNDAY. ALSO THURSDAY. ALSO NOW.
papers.subject: bandstands
papers.note: Anglers mind: more concerts by the water.

papers.text: Gilt the market bus stop. Then the bus. Then the notebooks.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Bus minds: their stop, bus and notebooks gilded for a display.

papers.text: Turn the Provincial Clock to the buses. Shops can go by the 8:15.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Clear the stalls on Sunday for the band. Then Saturday, to practise.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Is a band on a bus a concert or a bus? An inquiry, by field trip.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The band-bus inquiry asks for a second bus. The drum did not fit.

papers.text: Buy the Evening Fuss front page, nightly, for your face. Rodney has a few.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A desk fountain in your likeness. Fountains reflect so well on people.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the fountain: it asks for a bus shelter, to keep out of the rain.

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR GIVES FOUNTAIN A BUS SHELTER; SPOTTERS GET WET
clippings.refuse: FOUNTAIN STAYS ON DESK. DESK DAMP

papers.text: A bus shelter outside the hat shop. The hats may look through it.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Shops mind: the shelter stands in front of the display.

papers.text: Your Evening Fuss notices are 60 % bus times. A column for us?
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Till's Teas will hire the market scales: scones by the official ounce.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.note: Vegetables mind: the scales the growers use.

papers.text: Stand in our best window for an hour, Governor. As the display.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A working group on the growers' pound. Then the ounce. Then the dozen.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: Thirteen is now in doubt. The working group asks for a baker's dozen.

papers.text: A cuckoo for the Provincial Clock. Hourly, it says your name.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Another basket, like the first. Keep the ribbon round it. No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the ribbon: on concert day, it would like to go round the bandstand.

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR TIES UP BANDSTAND; BAND PLAYS ON THE GRASS
clippings.refuse: RIBBON RETURNED, STILL IN ITS BOW

papers.text: Add to each county signpost, under BUS STATION: OR, THE SHOPS.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Bus minds: their signpost now advertises the shops.

papers.text: Hats to the market's front, marrows to the back. Marrows can wait.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: We will sponsor the bus timetables. Each ends: SEE ALSO MARROWS.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Sign each prize certificate by hand, Governor. Onions like ink.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A bus stop right beside the bandstand. Every tune gets a bus in it.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Set-up to the premise: a new stop beside the bandstand. Brass minds: a bus every nine minutes through the concert.

papers.text: A signpost to you in every county. Then one on you, saying HERE.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: We will hire the allotments' top corner. Nine buses an hour pass it.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Vegetables mind: spotters standing among the beds (style 1's feud).

papers.text: Lend us the market scales on show day. Shops can guess, on a form.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The band will pay to list practice as an event. Wrong notes free.
papers.subject: bandstands
papers.note: Set-up to the premise. Anglers mind: practice by the water, now advertised.

papers.text: Ring the concert bell for the camera. Then stay to the end.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Proof the band is 30 % quieter than it sounds: a study, to be played.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The quiet study wants a louder edition. Nobody heard the first.

papers.text: A pumpkin shelter at the bus stop. Then a bench. Then the bus stop.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Lend the band the bus shelter on Sundays. Its audience is waiting.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Why no signpost points to the show: a study. Each fills in a form.
papers.subject: signage
papers.biggerStudy: The signpost study asks for a signpost to itself. It is hard to find.

papers.text: Hold our ceremonial float for the Evening Fuss. Neither of you may bob.
papers.subject: ceremonies
papers.note: Set-up to the premise. Brass mind: the Anglers in the paper, not the band.

papers.text: A committee to decide if the clock chimes a note, or the time.
papers.subject: clocks
papers.biggerStudy: The chime committee asks for one more chime, slowly, for the minutes.

papers.text: A second bandstand facing ours, so the band hears itself. Then a third.
papers.subject: bandstands
papers.note: Anglers mind: twice the band by the water.

papers.text: Unveil the new timetable. Read the 9:14 aloud, with feeling.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A committee on the echo. Its sign: ECHO, PLEASE WAIT YOUR TURN.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The echo committee asks to meet twice. Once, then slightly later.

papers.text: We will buy the five o'clock chime, to keep. The band starts on it.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: One bus horn a day at the river bridge. We will pick the honk.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Add QUIET, BAND to each county signpost. Small, as an example.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Pad the river bus shelter. A pencil carries 40 metres over water.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Bus mind: their shelter padded and muffled.
